## Module map

- `lib.rs` — `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, module declarations and re-exports
  only. No implementation code.
- `diagnostic.rs` — `Level`, `Diagnostic` (`{level, message, line, column,
  frame}`, §5b) and its JSON, keys in that order.
- `images.rs` — the decoded-image cache (spec §11 G-39, #127): `Asset
  {data, digest}`, a process-wide `Mutex` map from an asset's own SHA-256
  to `Ready`/`Building`/`Refused`/`Skipped {len}`, `set_image_cache_limit`,
  `image_cache_bytes`, the doc-hidden `image_cache_builds`, `cached_kind`,
  and the builder of a stored-deflate RGBA8 PNG copy, used only when it
  decodes to exactly the original's pixmap and `imagesize` reads the same
  size. No lock is held across a decode, an encode or a usvg call; a
  build writes only while its digest is still `Building`; the default limit
  is 0, so a binary that sets none takes the original route. The doc-hidden
  `set_image_build_hook` installs an `ImageBuildHook` every build calls
  between its two locks with none held, so a test can hold a build there.

  `load_system_fonts`, G-6) and the asset map (each asset keeps its own
  SHA-256; a PNG or JPEG kind is asked of the cache first), their content `version`
  (SHA-256 with length prefixes), the `measure_text` memo, and the
  crate-private `options()` builder whose resolvers record into a `Probe`
  what resvg never reports. The generic families map to bundled faces

  Mono, G-6), and `select_font` queries only the text's own families,
  never usvg's appended serif fallback, so a missing family still draws
  nothing and is warned.

  caller's strided buffer, and every warning text `rasterize` answers:

  attributes and `<style>` sheets, and the family of a `font` shorthand in

  the app shows them on the clip.

# Frame Job graphics — the API

A **graphic** is a motion graphic drawn by code: one JavaScript ES module
whose `render` returns an SVG string for each frame. Frame Job runs it in a
sandboxed QuickJS engine and rasterizes the SVG with resvg. The same frame
with the same props always draws the same pixels. A gradient is dithered
where it is rounded to 8 bits, by a fixed pattern of pixel position under
half a level, so dark gradients do not band; flat colours, images, text and
alpha are not. This page is the whole API. Every `js` block on it is run
by a test, so the examples work as written.

## The module

```js
export const meta = {
  name: "Lower third",        // shown in the inspector
  durationInFrames: 150,      // optional: the default length of a new clip
};

export const schema = {
  title:    { type: "string",  default: "Jane Doe", label: "Title" },
  subtitle: { type: "string",  default: "Director of Photography" },

|---|---|

| Bebas Neue | 400 |

installed.

for you. A family the set lacks draws nothing, with a warning naming the
families that are installed; in a list (`"Nope, Montserrat"`) the first
installed family draws.

## The sandbox

A graphic is a pure function of `frame`, `props`, `ctx` and its fonts and
assets. These refuse, with these sentences:

```text

`WebAssembly` or `Intl`. Modern syntax works: template literals, `??`, `?.`,
`**`, destructuring, `Array.prototype.at`, `replaceAll`, `findLast`.

## Limits

- **Time**: each call has a budget — 250 ms per frame in preview, 2 s in an
  export. The module's top level has one too. Over it, the answer is an
  error such as `over the 250 ms budget at frame 12 (InternalError:
  interrupted)`.

  error with a line and column.
- **Size**: a graphic draws at most 8192 pixels on a side.
- **The answer**: `render` must return an SVG string. `undefined` is
  ``render returned undefined at frame 12 — did you forget `return`?``.
  The string may be at most 8 MiB (8388608 bytes); a longer one is
  `render returned 9000000 bytes at frame 12; the SVG may be at most
  8388608 bytes`.

## Diagnostics

Every problem comes back as `{level, message, line, column, frame}`.
`level` is `"error"` (nothing drew) or `"warning"` (it drew anyway).
`line` and `column` are the module's own, when known; for a timeout they

content.content:
orig §10.1 q4, §10.4 G1b). resvg has no fallback with system fonts off, and
it does not report the miss. An unquoted family name with a digit-led word
(`Source Sans 3`) lays out nothing. So every standard-library helper quotes
family names, and `rasterize` warns about a family the set cannot resolve,
naming the families it has.

**The texture cache is keyed on the SVG TEXT plus size and library version,
not on the recipe hash** (orig §5d). A graphic that has settled on one frame
rasterizes once, and an edited file can never hit a stale texture. The
JavaScript still runs every frame; it is the cheapest of the three costs
(p95 ≤ 1.67 ms at 1080p). Graphic textures get their own LRU pool of six
(`LayerRenderers.graphicCacheLimit`), because a new 8–33 MB texture every
frame would evict every text and shape texture from the shared pool of 64.

**Parallel rendering, prefetch and a worker pool were not built in the road
map (G6)** (orig §1, §9 G6). The compositor and export were serial, and q3
measured the six samples at a worst p95 of 7.62 ms per frame at 1080p,
against a 12 ms line. At 4K, `title-card` measured 26 ms p95. The user
played graphics at 4K on an M2 Max, saw no stutter, and deferred G6. Since
issue #127 (2026-09-30, spec §11 G-26) an `ExportWriter` export rasterizes
its graphics ahead on worker threads (`GraphicPrefetch.swift`); the
compositor stays serial and the one writer, uses a worker's raster only on a
pool miss whose texture key matches its own, and still runs `svg`, records
every report and draws every card, so the file is the serial path's.
Since G6 phase 2 (2026-10-21, spec §11 G-36) a preview playing forward does
the same on the document's own key, its workers following the frame the

plan proposed, were rejected under `core/CLAUDE.md`'s rules.

## What it built — where it lives now

- `graphic/` — the crate. `src/`: `lib.rs`, `library.rs`, `raster.rs`,
  `measure.rs`, `module.rs`, `runtime.rs`, `sandbox.rs`, `exception.rs`,
  `host.rs`, `props.rs`, `diagnostic.rs`, `stdlib.js`, `noise.js`, `path.js`;
  rules in
  `graphic/CLAUDE.md`. `tests/graphics/` holds the six fixtures, which are
  also the Insert ▸ Graphic templates (copied into the bundle as
  `GraphicTemplates/` by `project.yml`).
- Core: `ffi_graphic.rs` (the ten exports; `read_bytes`/`free_boxed` in
  `ffi_util.rs`), `model_graphic.rs`, `edit_graphic.rs`, `recipe_graphic.rs`;
  arms in `edit_split.rs`, `edit_clip_timing.rs`, `edit_edge.rs` and
  `edit_action.rs` (`GRAPHIC_NOT_A_TARGET`); tests `core/tests/graphic.rs`,
  `graphic_ffi.rs`, `schema_v10.rs`.
- Header `core/include/framejob_core.h` (`/* graphics */` section); Swift
  wrappers at the end of `app/Sources/ReelCore.swift`. The size toll moved
  code out first, into `RecipeSource.swift` and `MediaDescriptor.swift`.
- App: `GraphicStore.swift` (+`Manual`, +`Import`), `GraphicScan.swift`,
  `GraphicRegistry.swift`, `LayerRenderersGraphic.swift`,
  `GraphicContactSheet.swift`, `GraphicTemplates.swift`,
  `ProjectDocument+Graphics.swift`, `ProjectSnapshot+Graphic.swift`,
  `ExporterGraphics.swift`, `ExporterErrors.swift`, `GraphicPane.swift`
  (+`Source`), `GraphicSchemaRows.swift`, `EditorViewController+Graphics.swift`
  and `+GraphicMenus.swift`, `AppDelegate+GraphicMenu.swift`,
  `AgentServer+Graphics.swift`, `+GraphicRender.swift`, `+GraphicImports.swift`,
  `AgentCatalog+Graphics.swift`.
- Docs: `docs/graphics-api.md`, `docs/graphics-api.d.ts`; `CONTEXT.md`
  terms Graphic, Module, Props, Revision.
- Proofs: `tools/proof/graphics_proof.py` (40 rows, the agent loop),
  `graphics_ffi_probe.py`, `graphics_store_probe.py`/`_proof.py`,
  `graphics_inspector_proof.py`, `graphics_menu_proof.py`,
  `graphics_pin_probe.swift`, `media_less_playback_probe.py`,
  `graphics_playback_samples.py`. The G0 spike's instruments are in
  `tools/proof/graphics_spike/`; do not re-run it, because it overwrites the
  recorded `work/` outputs.

## Known limits

- **Cost.** The app binary is about 7.9 MB larger, and QuickJS is kept even
  when nothing calls it. A cold build pays about 18 s for QuickJS's C.
- **Performance** was measured on one M2 Max only. The worst 1080p p95 was
  7.62 ms per frame; 4K `title-card` was 26 ms p95 (57 ms max). Rasterizing
  dominates, not the JavaScript. A slower machine or a heavier graphic is

orig §10.1 q4, §10.4 G1b). resvg has no fallback with system fonts off, and

(`Source Sans 3`) lays out nothing. So every standard-library helper quotes
family names, and `rasterize` warns about a family the set cannot resolve,
naming the families it has.

not on the recipe hash** (orig §5d). A graphic that has settled on one frame
rasterizes once, and an edited file can never hit a stale texture. The
JavaScript still runs every frame; it is the cheapest of the three costs

(`LayerRenderers.graphicCacheLimit`), because a new 8–33 MB texture every
frame would evict every text and shape texture from the shared pool of 64.

map (G6)** (orig §1, §9 G6). The compositor and export were serial, and q3

content.content:
graphic is drawn in, Frame Job adds a fixed, fine pattern under half a
  level, so a dark gradient shades smoothly instead of in steps. Flat
  colours, pictures, text and transparency are drawn exactly. The pattern
  survives `render_frame`, Save Frame… and ProRes. A 10-bit export
  (`hevc_10bit`) smooths most of it away but keeps the in-between shades,
  so the gradient stays smooth; an 8-bit H.264 or HEVC export smooths it
  away too, and its steps come back.

Module names use lowercase letters, digits and `-`, start with a letter or a
digit, and are at most 63 characters (`lower-third`, `title-2`).

Graphics draw only with the fonts bundled with Frame Job and the ones you add
to the project (see [Fonts and pictures](#fonts-and-pictures)), never with
the fonts installed on your Mac, so a project draws the same everywhere.

## Adding a graphic

**Insert ▸ Graphic** lists the bundled templates, then **From File…**:

| Item | What you get | Default length |
|---|---|---|
| Bar Chart | A titled bar chart whose bars grow in turn, from comma-separated values and labels | 150 frames |
| Callout | A circle that draws itself on, with an arrow and a label, at a position on the frame | 90 frames |
| Counter | A number counting from one value to another with thousands separators, a prefix and a label | 90 frames |
| Kinetic Type | A sentence shown word by word, each word springing in, with an accent colour | 150 frames |
| Lower Third | A name and subtitle that slide in and fade out, boxed or not, aligned left, centre or right | 150 frames |
| Title Card | A title fitted to the frame and a kicker over a two-colour gradient, fading in and out | 120 frames |
| From File… | Asks for a `.js` module and copies it into the project | the module's own |

Each template's properties, as the Graphic sub-tab shows them:

| Template | Properties |
|---|---|
| Bar Chart | values and labels (comma-separated text), title, color |
| Callout | x and y (sliders from 0 to 1, a fraction of the frame's width and height), label, color |
| Counter | from, to, prefix, label, color |
| Kinetic Type | text, stagger (1–30), color, accent |

- **G-16 — Insert ▸ Graphic: where the clip goes, what the module is
  called, and what a module that does not compile does** (road map 10
  §10.9 G5b, 2026-09-25). Insert ▸ Graphic is `write_graphic` of a template
  or a chosen `.js`, then `add_graphic_clip` at the module's `meta`

  overwrites a module another clip draws. Duplicate as New Graphic…'s

**MOT-1 — Motion presets**
- **Do:** 1. Apply each Clip ▸ Motion preset (In, Out, During) at ordinary clip lengths; use Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Preview. 2. Drag a clip on the canvas mid-motion. 3. Look at the timeline wedges at S, M and L. 4. Apply `spin`, and a slide inside a nest.
- **Expect:** the numbers feel right; `pop` reads as a pop; Preview loops the clip; a mid-motion drag is tolerable; wedges read at every height; `spin` turns the way the preset table says; the slide leaves by the nest's edge.
- **Source:** #54.

## Graphics

Uses the four `tools/proof/work/playback-check/` projects (Setup 3).

**GR-1 — Graphics play, watched**
- **Do:** 1. Open `Playback-1080p` at Preview Quality Full; play. 2. In each of `Playback-1080p`, `Playback-4K` and `Error-card`: play, scrub, and loop an in/out range.
- **Expect:** `lower-third` and `kinetic-type` play smoothly; with no video beneath, the preview shows, Play runs, and scrub and loop look right.
- **Source:** #56.

**GR-2 — Memory at 4K, and a slower machine**
- **Do:** 1. Play `Playback-4K` with Activity Monitor open on Frame Job's memory. 2. If one is available, play it on a slower Mac, or a heavier graphic.
- **Expect / Answer:** memory stays steady (note the figure); no stutter. A stutter goes on #127 with the project and the machine: playback rasterizes graphics ahead (spec §11 G-36), so a stutter is graphics performance work again.
- **Source:** #56.

**GR-3 — The error card**
- **Do:** Open `Error-card` and play past 2 s.

# Manual checks

The standing list of checks only a person at the machine can do: things
that need eyes, ears, a real mouse and keyboard, a second display, a real
network, a real API key or macOS permissions. Everything a script can
measure is already in `tools/proof/` and is not repeated here.

**When to run it.** Run every section before a release. Between releases,
run the sections whose area changed. Unless a check says otherwise, run it
in both appearances (System Settings ▸ Appearance, Light then Dark).

## Setup, once per run
- **Source:** #127 G6 phase 4 (spec §11 G-38); `tools/proof/background_render_proof.py` measures this by tool, not the keyboard path or the look.

**GR-12 — A dark gradient graphic shows no rings and no visible grain**
- **Setup:** a 1920×1080 project; your usual display brightness; View ▸ Preview Quality ▸ Full.
- **Do:** Insert ▸ Graphic ▸ From File… a module that fills the frame with a dark radial gradient, e.g. `raster_dither_proof.py`'s `band374` (`<radialGradient gradientUnits="userSpaceOnUse" cx="960" cy="540" r="1100">`, `#2A4F3D` at the centre to `#0D1512` at the edge). Look at it in the preview, then save the frame (File ▸ Save Frame… as PNG) and open it in Preview at 100 %. Export it as `prores_422` and as `hevc_10bit`, and once as `h264`, and look at each in QuickTime Player at 100 %.
- **Expect:** in the preview, the saved PNG, the ProRes and the `hevc_10bit` file the gradient shades smoothly, with no rings or steps you can pick out, and no grain you can see at 100 % from your normal distance. The `h264` file may show its steps again: that is PR-13's recorded limit, not a defect.
- **Answer:** rings in the preview, yes or no; rings in the PNG, the ProRes, the `hevc_10bit`, the `h264`, each yes or no; visible grain anywhere, yes or no (and where).
- **Source:** #375 part 1 (spec §11 PR-13); `tools/proof/raster_dither_proof.py` measures the banding (B1–B4b) and the per-pixel noise each export keeps, not how it looks to a person on a display.

## Mattes

"""Road map 10, G5b — Insert ▸ Graphic (the bundled templates and From
File…), File ▸ Add Font to Graphics… and Add Image to Graphics…, Help ▸
Graphics Reference — and issue batch B84's phase 2 (#103, spec §11 G-30):
File ▸ Rename Graphic…, Delete Graphic… and Restore Graphic Version… and
their one sheet — against the built app and a probe.

    python3 tools/proof/graphics_menu_proof.py [--app PATH]
    python3 tools/proof/graphics_menu_proof.py --mutant <name>

**The instance.** ONE instance of the built app (`proof_app`'s choice) for the run, on a scratch socket of
its own, launched and stopped by PID, **in a scratch home**
(`CFFIXED_USER_HOME=tools/proof/work/graphics-menu/home`, the way
`graphics_files_proof.py` launches), its log at
`work/graphics-menu/framejob.log`. No persisting menu item is performed and
no sheet is confirmed over MCP. At the start and at exit the home, the
packages, the captures and a mutant's tree copy are removed; what stays in
`work/graphics-menu/` is the probe's build (`probe/`) and the last log.

    args = parser.parse_args()
    app = Path(args.app)
    WORK.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    remove_leftovers()
    atexit.register(remove_leftovers)
    if args.mutant in PROBE_MUTANTS:
        return probe_mutant(app, args.mutant)
    if args.mutant in APP_MUTANTS:
        return app_mutant(args.mutant)
    print("Road map 10, G5b and B84 phase 2 — the graphics menus, templates and file sheet",
          flush=True)
    if not app.exists():
        check("the app is built", False, str(app))
        print(f"\n0/{len(RESULTS)} checks passed")
        return 1
    print("\n0 — the bundle, the instance and the fixtures over MCP", flush=True)
    bundle_check(app)

    def rows(client, gm, gf, facts):
        probe_checks(gm, gf)
        sheet_rows(client, gf, facts)

    session(app, rows)
    good = sum(1 for _, ok in RESULTS if ok)
    print(f"\n{good}/{len(RESULTS)} checks passed")
    return 0 if RESULTS and good == len(RESULTS) else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

content.content:
### Paths: `getLength(d)`, `getPointAtLength(d, length)` and `evolvePath(progress, d)`

`d` is SVG path data: every command (`M L H V C S Q T A Z`) and its
relative form. `getLength` answers the path's length, curves and arcs
measured to within about 0.01 %. `getPointAtLength` answers `{x, y, angle}`:
the point that far along the path (`length` is clamped to the path) and the
way the path is heading there, in degrees, ready for `rotate()`.
`evolvePath` answers `{strokeDasharray, strokeDashoffset}` for a `progress`
of 0–1: put both on the `<path>` and it is drawn from its start up to that
fraction. Its dash is 0.1 % longer than the measured length, so a closed
outline closes at 1.

A path of several pieces (more than one `M`) draws them all at once, each
from its own start and at the same speed, the longest finishing at 1; pieces
drawn one after another are one `<path>` each. A path that cannot be read
throws, naming where reading stopped —
`getLength: cannot parse the path at character 6: "X 5 5"` — and is never a
silent zero. A number too large to do arithmetic with (`1e999`, or a line
1e200 long, whose square overflows) is refused in the same sentence, so no
answer is ever `Infinity` or `NaN`.

The paths a graphic measures are remembered, so the same `d` costs a lookup
on later calls and frames — up to 32 paths, and about 50,000 characters and
measured pieces between them (a curve is 64 pieces). Past either limit all
are forgotten and measured again when next asked for, so with paths that
large take every length and point from one before turning to the next.

```js
const d = `M 200 ${ctx.height / 2} C 600 100 1000 900 1400 ${ctx.height / 2}`;
const total = getLength(d);
const tip = getPointAtLength(d, total * ctx.progress);
const dash = evolvePath(ctx.progress, d);
const line = `<path d="${d}" fill="none" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="8"
  stroke-dasharray="${dash.strokeDasharray}" stroke-dashoffset="${dash.strokeDashoffset}"/>
  <circle cx="${tip.x}" cy="${tip.y}" r="12" fill="#ffcc00"/>`;
```

### `measureText(text, font)`

`font` is `{family, size, weight, style, letterSpacing, xmlSpace}`
(defaults Montserrat, 16, 400, `"normal"`, 0, `"default"`). Answers
`{width, ascent, descent, lineHeight, inkX, inkWidth}`: `width` is the
advance (where the next word starts); `inkX` / `inkWidth` are the drawn
glyphs. With `xmlSpace: "default"` runs of spaces collapse as SVG draws
them; with `"preserve"` a run of spaces beside a drawn glyph counts, as
`xml:space="preserve"` draws it, and any other value throws. Text that is
only whitespace measures zero either way. A family that is not installed
throws, naming the families that are.

```js
const m = measureText("Hello", { family: "Montserrat", size: 64, weight: 800 });
const boxWidth = m.width + 80;
const gap = measureText("a  b", { family: "sans-serif", size: 48, xmlSpace: "preserve" });
```

### `wrapText(text, maxWidth, font)`

Lines that each fit `maxWidth`; a word longer than the width breaks by
characters.

```js
const lines = wrapText("A title long enough to need two lines", 600,
  { family: "Source Sans 3", size: 64, weight: 700 });
```

### `fitText(text, maxWidth, font, {min = 8, max = 400})`

The largest whole font size at which `text` fits `maxWidth` on one line.

```js
const size = fitText("BREAKING", ctx.width - 200, { family: "Anton" }, { max: 300 });
```

### `textLines(lines, {x, y, lineHeight, anchor, fill, font})`

A `<text>` with one `<tspan>` per line, the family QUOTED for you (a CSS
generic such as `sans-serif` is written bare, as it must be).
`anchor` is `"start"`, `"middle"` or `"end"`; `lineHeight` defaults to
1.2 × the size. A font with `xmlSpace: "preserve"` writes
`xml:space="preserve"` on the `<text>`, so it draws the spaces `measureText`
counted; a `style` of `"italic"` or `"oblique"` and a non-zero
`letterSpacing` are written as `font-style` and `letter-spacing`, so it draws
the font `wrapText` broke the lines with.

```js
const font = { family: "Source Sans 3", size: 48, weight: 600 };
const body = textLines(wrapText("Two short lines of text", 400, font),
  { x: 100, y: 200, anchor: "start", fill: "#ffffff", font });
const code = textLines(["let  x = 1;"],
  { x: 100, y: 300, font: { family: "monospace", size: 32, xmlSpace: "preserve" } });
```

## Approach
1. Append G-44 to `designs/spec/11-decisions/graphics.md`. The bundled templates: (a) `u = Math.min(ctx.width, ctx.height) / 1080`, the six's `ctx.height / 1080` in landscape; (b) everything at every frame inside the 90 % title-safe rect, entrances by spring, clipPath or fade and never from off-frame; (c) a card's background is static from frame 0; (d) Montserrat 800/900 for text, IBM Plex Mono 500 for ticking digits, `'Source Sans 3'` 600 only for window-frame's UI text; (e) generic vector glyphs only, no brand artwork; (f) an `accent` colour, and an outro in the last ~15 frames keyed to `ctx.durationInFrames`; (g) `tests/templates.rs` holds every non-fixture template to (b) and (c) at both orientations. Update the index row and Lines cell.
2. Write `templates.rs` first, with the PNG dump.
3. Write the 17 modules, one category at a time. For each: run the targeted test with `GRAPHIC_TEMPLATE_PNGS=…/tools/proof/work/graphics-templates`, Read the PNGs (entrance, hold, outro, both orientations), and iterate until they look professional (spacing, hierarchy, alignment, no clipping or overlap).
4. Make the project.yml, proof, probe, README, guide, menus, spec and CLAUDE.md edits, and add the manual-checks row.
5. Mutants (temporary edits, each reverted): (m1) a 4×4 rect at (10, 10) in gauge → test fails; (m2) chapter-card's background fades in → it fails; (m3) `font-family="Nope"` in step-badge → it fails; (m4) drop one stem from project.yml → `project_yml_lists_every_template` fails; (m5) wantTitles with 22 entries → M2 fails.
6. `make gate`, then the Release proof.

## Constraints
- Follow the six (`graphic/tests/graphics/lower-third.js` for panels `#101014`@0.82, text `#ffffff`, secondary `#d8d8e0`; `callout.js` for draw-on and arrows; `counter.js` for `formatNumber`). Use the stdlib helpers in `docs/graphics-api.md` (`spring`, `interpolate`, `Easing`, `evolvePath`, `measureText`, `wrapText`, `fitText`, `escapeXml`, `formatNumber`, `asset`). Quote `'Source Sans 3'`. Put every prop that reaches markup through `escapeXml`. No `Math.random` (use `random(seed)`).
- Parse comma lists as bar-chart does: non-finite values dropped, and an empty list draws the frame without throwing.
- Fit long user text with `fitText`/`wrapText` against the safe width, so defaults and longer strings stay inside.
- `GraphicTemplates.list(in:)` (`app/Sources/GraphicTemplates.swift`) accepts only stems for which `GraphicStore.isModuleName` is true. All 17 stems are. Insert ▸ Graphic (`app/Sources/AppDelegate+GraphicMenu.swift`) sorts them by stem.
- `graphic/tests/common/mod.rs`'s FIXTURES, `pins.json` and the pin, render and determinism tests stay on the six. Re-pinning is out of bounds.
- `tools/proof/spec_index_proof.py` (in `make test`) checks every Lines cell against `wc -l`. `name_residue.py` (gate) reads every file.
- The worktree only. No commit, push or merge.
